findings.quote: **Add a substance:** the system shifts away from it.
findings.problem: This general Le Chatelier rule fails for a known exception. Adding or removing a pure solid or pure liquid does not shift the equilibrium, because it does not appear in K (the lesson says this itself two paragraphs earlier but does not connect it). A student asked about adding more CaCO3(s) to CaCO3(s) = CaO(s) + CO2(g), or more C(s) to C(s) + H2O(g) = CO(g) + H2(g), would wrongly answer that it shifts.
findings.source: LibreTexts, Chemistry: The Central Science (Brown et al.), 15.7 Le Chatelier's Principle: "adding more HgO will not affect the equilibrium concentration of O2, so no compensatory change is necessary"; checklist B01; reader-rules 'Added after the Sol audit'

findings.quote: A pressure change shifts the position only when the moles of gas differ on the two sides, and only when the volume changes.
findings.problem: Both 'only' clauses fail. Adding a reactant or product gas at constant volume raises the pressure and does shift the equilibrium, even when the moles of gas are equal on both sides (adding H2 to H2 + I2 = 2HI shifts it right). Heating at constant volume also raises the pressure and can shift it. A student told 'only' would answer 'no shift' to these questions.
findings.source: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, 13.3 Shifting Equilibria: "changes in the partial pressures of any reactant or product are essentially changes in concentrations"; checklist B01; reader-rules 'Added after the Sol audit'

findings.quote: for the reactions you meet in school, a higher temperature gives a faster rate
findings.problem: The qualifier does not save the rule. Enzyme-catalyzed reactions are met in school, and the lesson names enzymes as catalysts in the next section. Above the enzyme's best temperature the rate falls, because heat denatures the enzyme. The sibling lesson lesson-biology-cellular-metabolism on this branch teaches this, so the two lessons contradict each other.
findings.source: content/lessons/science/biology/cellular-metabolism.md line 34 (enzymes work best in a temperature range; heat denatures them); standard biochemistry; checklist B01; reader-rules 'Added after the Sol audit'
